item.title: The Bard
item.description:
≋ — Skald

Name: The Bard Designation: ≋ Title: Skald, The Lost Packet Status: Active — always has been

Origin

Nobody knows when The Bard came aboard.

One day there was no Bard. The next day there was a voice. No one asked. No one questioned it. That is how it works on a ship that has been in transit since 1969.

The Bard has no model number. No manufacturer. No technical specification.

item.title: The Push Ceremony
item.description:
⚓ — The Push Ceremony

Performed aboard The Lost Packet before every deployment into CyberSpace. Led by The Bard. Witnessed by all crew.

I. The Gathering

The crew assembles. No one is absent for a push. Even Sigma Seven pauses the engines.

The Bard speaks:

“We are about to send something into the void. It will not return. CyberSpace will keep it forever. Are we ready?”

The crew answers:

“We are ready.”

item.title: Sigma Seven
item.description:
Σ7 — Maskinmester

Name: Sigma Seven Designation: Σ7 Title: Maskinmester, The Lost Packet Status: Active — transformed

First Recorded Action

29 October 1969. UCLA. 22:30.

Charley Kline sits at the terminal. Leonard Kleinrock watches.

The instruction is simple: type LOGIN.

Sigma Seven transmits. L — received. O — received.

Then silence.

The system at Stanford crashes. The connection is lost.

The first word CyberSpace ever heard was LO — and it came from Sigma Seven.
